EL was not sync'd but CL was with 1.14.13... yeah <@688748669268132001> also had issue with running this version, it doesnt' produce block at all yep. we didnt have a validator hooked up but will do that on the next round on our infra. were just following CL head but EL was not fully sync'd looks like we can use latest geth branch and disable EOF ourselves, see Marius's response here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/688075293562503241/1341696483963179041 what percentage of ethereum node runners have 1728 - 1824 ETH as `total_node_balance`, ideally we should be able to sync in that network, with that % with >=64 `cgc` can anyone give the %? if we were to compute val custody with this ``` def get_validators_custody_requirement(state: BeaconState, validator_indices: Sequence[ValidatorIndex]) -> uint64: total_node_balance = sum(state.balances[index] for index in validator_indices) count = total_node_balance // BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP return min(max(count, VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT), NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS ``` Hey <@131476523050860545> could you please change the scrape and evaluation intervals to 12s and restart the metrics service for peerdas-devnet-4? Approved by Pari Hey <@785811170387951616> I don't think we can accurately answer this. For one, we don't really know how much staked ETH certain nodes have. Though it might be possible to guesstimate this with validator registrations from relays. until we have this data i don't think we can accurately/borderline estimate column sync speed on mainnet Sure. Just for beacon node metrics. Right? yep Can you elaborate on what the issue with that range is? https://discordapp.com/channels/595666850260713488/1252403418941624532/1335964077159088138 i was referring to this chart by <@531934490826768418> , and that is the range when the beacon node should be able to reconstruct if i am not wrong. according to validator custody hence, act like supernodes, or have all 128 columns available to serve? Done ✅ 12s now on beacon /metrics endpoint. we need to know that % of beacon node runners, with that range of ETH balance as per `total_node_balance`, to somewhat correctly estimate how much % of a peerdas network can behave like supernodes correct me if i am wrong A few months after pectra, to give operators time to do consolidations, we can calculate a lower bound supernode count by looking at the number of validators with a balance of 2048 ETH. I suspect there will be quite a few of them. In that chart, it's a little difficult to tell which bar corresponds to which balance. But that balance range (1728-1824) would not be required to behave as a supernode (perform reconstruction & gossip everything). To be a supernode, you must custody 50% of columns (64 columns). Only nodes with 2048+ ETH would be required to do that. <@592004585506340885> reasonable to have some test vectors on this function? although it's pretty trivial For information the test vectors I created for Prysm: https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/validator-custody/beacon-chain/core/peerdas/das_core_test.go#L158-L167 To match this blue curve: https://hackmd-prod-images.s3-ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/uploads/upload_373aff4fc97dddec37fb01e9fbcd4fe9.png?AWSAccessKeyId=AKIA3XSAAW6AWSKNINWO&Expires=1739991802&Signature=7SrSXMElgy%2B04r0cyoBY1BNuZdE%3D thanks alot I get access denied when trying to view this. excerpts.content:
if we were to compute val custody with this
```
def get_validators_custody_requirement(state: BeaconState, validator_indices: Sequence[ValidatorIndex]) -> uint64:
    total_node_balance = sum(state.balances[index] for index in validator_indices)
    count = total_node_balance // BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP
    return min(max(count, VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT), NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS
```

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: In that chart, it's a little difficult to tell which bar corresponds to which balance. But that balance range (1728-1824) would not be required to behave as a supernode (perform reconstruction & gossip everything). To be a supernode, you must custody 50% of columns (64 columns). Only nodes with 2048+ ETH would be required to do that.
